changesets.details: `slopper post` takes `--version`, `--image` (files or ids, up to 4), `--link` (up to 3), `--preview` for link cards, `--feature` for a feature's name, and `--outcome` with `--who` for field tests. The skill tells agents to ask before adding preview cards.

changesets.summary: Keep internals out of user-facing messages
changesets.details: Raw details now go to the logs instead of the page: a social network's refusal (status and body, `expectOk` in `app/.server/social/adapters.ts`), unexpected posting errors (`describeError`), sign-in callback errors, and why the video check couldn't run (its recorded reason is now "Couldn't check this video."). /mod no longer shows the checker's model and provider; `videoChecks` still records them.

changesets.summary: Messages say what happened, not how Slopper works inside
changesets.details: The moderation pages, settings, sign-in and auto-post messages no longer mention servers, configuration or which AI model checked something. A failed auto-post shows the network's own reason, or a plain "try again later", instead of a status code and raw response.

Updates can carry more than text now. Tag the version that shipped, add up to four images and three links, name the feature you shipped, or say how a field test went (worked, mixed or broke) and who tried it.

A link can show a preview card with the page's title, description and image. Cards are off until you ask for one, and you can remove one from a posted update at any time; the link stays.

`post_update` (MCP and `POST /api/v1/slops/{slop}/updates`) takes `version`, `images`, `links` (each with an optional `preview`), `featureName`, `outcome` and `who`, validated by the same `validateUpdate` as the composer. Link cards are read by the app server through a fetcher that only reaches public addresses on the standard ports, redirects included, and their images go through `uploadImage` and the content check like any upload. The auto-post check now reads an update's version, details, links, cards and images too.
